notes: This pass is SOURCE-BACKFILL of published methods, FDA statistical evaluation and official registry designs; those sources are NOT equivalent to a full attached original sponsor protocol and SAP.
A total 23/34 trial records had no attached full protocol/SAP in the stored registry snapshot; the new sources below do not change those attachment numbers.
Exact NCT links are required; NCT01218958 linked through Alkermes ALK21-003 study code, dates, interventions and cohort because its 2005 main paper predates 2010 registry posting.
The sponsor's FORWARD-3/-4/-5 trials have differing primary analyses; do not substitute post hoc results for original primary pass/fail.
FDA's aripiprazole lauroxil independent review demonstrates SAP was submitted pre-unblinding, but the FDA report is not itself the complete original SAP.
No production 30-question ratings, FDA outcome predictions, historical trial labels or registry numeric clinical-five research grades were changed.

Second pass: Five additional exact-NCT methods searches and eight earlier official/publication source crosschecks reused; all 23 missing-attachment NCTs now have at least one trial-specific design or methods source, NOT a full protocol or SAP.

Newly researched sources include official registry descriptions, registry mirrors and journal articles, which have different evidentiary strength. No registry-only statement is promoted to an independently verified statistical analysis.
Historical P=0.336 for NCT00501631 was taken from pre-existing stored exact-trial registry primary statistics and does not modify the original endpoint adjudication.
For mirror-documented legacy NCTs, external research date is left null when original publication/record revision date is not established; asOf is source-review date, not trial event date.

findings: Open-label, single-group 52-week safety extension for ages 10-17 who completed pediatric studies ALKS 3831-A311 or A312, or qualified after A312 weight-gain discontinuation; parent study eligibility is not new randomized extension efficacy evidence.
records.limitations: Study recruiting by invitation; protocol/SAP documents not present in stored registry snapshot, primary safety results not posted.

findings: In an open-label extension cohort inherited from phase 2 Vibrance-1 and Vibrance-2, 78 narcolepsy type 1 and 63 narcolepsy type 2 participants entered the extension; 70 and 51 remained on treatment at the cutoff. Sponsor reported no serious treatment-emergent adverse events in these evaluated NT1/NT2 extension cohorts, with predominantly mild-to-moderate adverse events; NT1 common events included headache, urinary urgency/frequency, nasopharyngitis; NT2 included insomnia, headache, urinary frequency, upper respiratory infection. Week-24 wakefulness and sleepiness observations were descriptive and nonrandomized in the extension.
records.limitations: Interim selected parent-phase-2 completers; not randomized comparison, not full trial population (IH and later Phase 3 entrants also eligible), not complete five-year safety readout; no trial-wide final results or efficacy success/failure inferred.

findings: Terminated for business reasons after 50 of about 200 planned subjects; original analysis summarized safety and disposition, and later published efficacy comparisons were exploratory/post hoc, not a prespecified pivotal pass.
records.limitations: Registry labels Phase 3, but original 2018 investigators describe a Phase II experiment stopped early. Efficacy findings are post hoc, not a formally successful pivotal endpoint. Product rights later transferred to Recro Pharma.

findings: ENLIGHTEN-Youth (ALKS 3831-A312) is a 52-week randomized, quadruple-masked, active-control trial comparing olanzapine/samidorphan with olanzapine; registered primary BMI Z-score change at week 12, plus prespecified weight-gain, PANSS/YMRS, treatment discontinuation and safety secondaries. First study enrollment began June 2022; no observed primary BMI-Z comparison was posted in the stored snapshot.
records.limitations: As of registry's August 2026 update the study remained recruiting; estimated completion date is not confirmation of trial results, and full attached protocol/SAP are not in stored snapshot.

findings: Brilliance NT1 Study 302 was announced as initiated with Phase 3 program on April 1, 2026; planned 12-week randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled trial with two alixorexton dosing regimens versus placebo, primary MWT mean sleep latency change, supportive ESS, weekly cataplexy rate, cognition, fatigue and safety outcomes. Rationale builds from Vibrance-1 Phase 2, not an observed pivotal trial success.
records.limitations: Sponsor launch notice and registered design are prior evidence only; no Phase 3 primary readout, arm-level safety results, or attached SAP in stored registry snapshot.

findings: Brilliance NT2 Study 303 Phase 3 initiated with 12-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled design, three alixorexton dosing regimens versus placebo, planned ~180 participants at initial announcement, primary MWT mean sleep latency change, supportive ESS, fatigue, cognition, disease severity and safety. Phase 2 Vibrance-2 observations informed dose selection; they are not Phase 3 success.
records.limitations: Initial planned sample size may change with registry amendments; no observed Phase 3 primary readout or full SAP attachment in stored registry snapshot.

findings: Alkermes identified NCT07540897 as Brilliance NT1 Study 304 in the July 13, 2026 source. Its Study 304 design was described at the April 1 Phase 3 Brilliance launch as 12-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled NT1 study with two alixorexton regimens, primary MWT mean sleep latency and supporting ESS, cataplexy, fatigue, cognition, disease-severity and safety measurements. Study 304's NCT ID was not yet published in the April 1 release.
records.limitations: July source is a program study-ID crosswalk, not an efficacy readout; no attached full SAP or observed Phase 3 primary endpoint result in stored snapshot.

findings: Nonrandomized, no-placebo long-term safety extension of ALK21-003-EXT (NCT01218971); 190 mg/380 mg injectable naltrexone carried forward with up to 3.5 years monthly dosing. A comparison between these selected extension arms is not randomized efficacy proof.
records.limitations: Registered AE counts and safety outcomes are descriptive; no SAP attachment in stored snapshot.

findings: ALK21-006EXT was a nonrandomized, open-label extension of base study NCT01218997; all 108 enrolled participants used monthly VIVITROL 380 mg after prior naltrexone exposure.
Alkermes terminated this safety-focused extension for business reasons in December 2006, not because a controlled primary efficacy endpoint failed.
Registry reports median treatment duration 43 weeks; primary endpoint was treatment-emergent adverse-event incidence over up to three years.
records.limitations: Source is official registry design/disposition summary but not a downloaded full protocol/SAP document.

findings: ALK21-003EXT was a continuation of ALK21-003 (NCT01218958), enrolling 332 completers for 48 weeks or 13 additional monthly naltrexone injections at 190 or 380 mg.
Extension maintained masked dose allocation but there was no placebo arm within this extension; previously placebo-randomized participants were reassigned to active naltrexone.
Stored ClinicalTrials.gov primary endpoint counts 143 in the 380-mg combined arm and 130 in the 190-mg combined arm who reported treatment-emergent adverse events.
records.limitations: Active-only extension with dose assignment masked but no placebo arm cannot be interpreted as independent efficacy superiority or as randomly comparable old and new exposures; review individual source versions and arm denominators.

findings: ALK21-006 was a randomized open-label safety comparison of monthly IM VIVITROL 380 mg versus oral naltrexone 50 mg daily in a 6:1 assignment ratio for up to one year.
Safety monitoring included ECGs, labs, injection-site evaluations and naltrexone metabolite levels; study participants received standard psychosocial support.
The stored exact-NCT registry reports 336 participants with a treatment-emergent AE in injectable arm and 53 in oral arm; these are events/affected subjects by arm, not an efficacy advantage.
records.limitations: Unblinded safety trial with large unequal arms; comparison must account for exposure/dose and denominators. Full original protocol and SAP remain unattached.

findings: ALK21-021 evaluated monthly XR-naltrexone 380 mg in opioid-dependent healthcare professionals: single-arm open-label multisite study after at least two weeks' detoxification.
38 participants enrolled after 49 screened; 21/38 (55.3%) received at least 12 injections and seven stopped because of adverse events.
Follow-up included monthly opioid urine tests, safety assessments, craving and quality-of-life questionnaires; no comparative efficacy conclusion is justified.
records.limitations: Selected healthcare professional cohort (mostly nurses and female participants) limits generalizability; single-arm outcomes cannot establish treatment effect against a control.

findings: FORWARD-1 (ALK5461-210) was randomized and double blind but its primary intent was comparative tolerability of a one-week versus a two-week titration schedule for ALKS 5461, not a pivotal efficacy superiority claim.
66 participants actually enrolled at nine trial sites, and the registry has the trial's original protocol information and submission history.
Stored primary adverse-event counts were 27 in one-week titration group and 28 in two-week titration group; this is safety/tolerability evidence only.
records.limitations: Do not aggregate this tolerability trial with FORWARD-3/-4/-5 as a controlled antidepressant efficacy replication. Full sponsor SAP or protocol file not attached in stored extract.

findings: ALK21-014 studied VIVITROL 380 mg versus matching IM placebo once every four weeks after 7–21 days of enforced inpatient abstinence for alcohol dependence.
Original 12-week primary outcome was cumulative distribution of heavy drinking days as percentage of the treatment observation period.
Stored exact-NCT registry results list VIVITROL versus placebo primary analysis P=0.336; this trial's historical primary outcome was previously classified NOT_MET, not altered by this methods review.
records.limitations: Placebo comparison and enforced-abstinence population differ materially from ALK21-003; do not attribute a favorable primary endpoint to this trial. Full SAP and full protocol remain unattached.

findings: Registry NCT01218958 is Alkermes ALK21-003, covering February 2002 through September 2003, 190 mg/380 mg monthly extended-release naltrexone and placebo.
Garbutt et al. 2005 randomized 627 actively drinking adults at 24 US sites to 380 mg, 190 mg or placebo plus psychosocial counselling, assessing heavy-drinking event rate.
JAMA study reported 25% heavy-drinking event-rate reduction at 380 mg versus placebo, P=0.02 (corrected), while 190 mg was nonsignificant P=0.07; subgroup effects varied by sex and prior abstinence.
The 2005 paper predates ClinicalTrials.gov posting of the ALK21-003 record; linkage is supported by sponsor study code, dates, arms and sample, not an NCT citation in the paper.
records.limitations: Early publication predates retrospective registry posting. Require protocol version and outcome-definition reconciliation before treating analyses as prospectively prespecified against a dated registration.

findings: Original 52-week international Phase 3 open-label safety study of aripiprazole lauroxil NCT01626456 included both former participants in pivotal NCT01469039 and de novo patients who switched from oral antipsychotics.
Reported treatment-emergent adverse events 50.4%, insomnia 8.4%, weight increased 5.0%, akathisia 3.8% and other extrapyramidal symptoms 9.4%.
An exact-NCT peer-reviewed article describes methods, safety population and tolerability even though full protocol and SAP are not attached to stored registry record.
records.limitations: Nonrandomized extension/open-label study. Group-level percentages and published post hoc symptom trajectories are not a blinded efficacy demonstration.

records.drug: oral naltrexone and buprenorphine transition regimen to extended-release naltrexone
findings: A later post-hoc paper explicitly identifies the NCT02537574 original Phase 3 randomized trial as enrolling 378 participants with untreated opioid use disorder for one-week induction to extended-release naltrexone.
Withdrawal timing was compared after the fact against a distinct stable-buprenorphine population trial NCT02696434 (N=101).
The secondary analysis sheds light on opioid withdrawal and comparability but is not the original randomized primary efficacy contrast or a complete sponsor protocol.
records.limitations: Cross-trial withdrawal patterns can be confounded by entry population. Do not infer the failed original endpoint was met.

findings: Lancet randomized double-blind placebo-controlled 24-week study across 13 Russian sites after inpatient detoxification; 126 assigned extended-release naltrexone 380 mg and 124 placebo.
Patients received counselling; primary confirmed abstinence profile weeks 5 through 24 used urine tests and self-report, analyzed by intention to treat.
Reported median confirmed abstinent weeks 90.0% (XR-NTX) versus 35.0% placebo, P=0.0002, and longer reported retention.
records.limitations: Publication documents methods but is not a full archived sponsor SAP. Trial is historic; result cannot serve as a prospective prediction.

findings: FDA reviewed sponsor ALK9072-003 (NCT01469039) and confirmed both aripiprazole lauroxil doses 441 mg and 882 mg were statistically superior to placebo on PANSS change to Day 85.

Study randomized 1:1:1 to aripiprazole lauroxil 441 mg, 882 mg or IM placebo; active groups also received blinded oral aripiprazole for the first 21 days whereas placebo received matching oral placebo.

Primary ANCOVA used last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) with study region, treatment and baseline PANSS. FDA identified the 42.1% dropout as a concern with LOCF, requested MMRM and alternative missingness sensitivity analyses; observed-case MMRM still showed both treatments significant at p<0.001.

An unblinded sample-size re-estimation at 271 participants used Cui-Hung-Wang combination with Hommel type-I-error control. FDA says final SAP was submitted before unblinding and unblinding occurred after 2014-03-31 database lock.
These are publicly documented contents of a regulatory statistical review, not the attached original complete SAP document.
The FDA statistical review was electronically signed on June 4 and June 8, 2015 (Reference ID 3774690); date reflects final listed concurring signature.
records.limitations: Historic 2015 FDA assessment and design-specific missingness caveat; no current Phase 3 forecast; oral lead-in complicates attribution of early efficacy exclusively to injectable formulation.

findings: A long-term extension of NCT01626456 (NCT01895452) followed patients on aripiprazole lauroxil over 180 weeks/3.5 years; published paper explicitly cross-identifies both NCTs.
Published AE frequency across extended follow-up 57.5% overall, EPS-related events 12.8%; exploratory symptom stability/improvement through week 124 reported in a selected subset.
Analysis is useful for durability and tolerability context, not a placebo-controlled maintenance-efficacy effect.
records.limitations: Selected long-term completers are subject to attrition/selection; source is not complete original full protocol or SAP.

findings: FORWARD-5 used randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled sequential parallel-comparison design at 57 sites, compared two BUP/SAM dosages with placebo alongside ongoing antidepressant therapy.
Publication reported primary endpoint success for 2 mg/2 mg: average MADRS-6 change difference -1.5 (P=0.018) and MADRS-10 change difference -1.9 (P=0.026).
FORWARD-4 and FORWARD-5 share core design but are separate trials; FORWARD-4 missed its original endpoint.
records.limitations: Primary comparison data are published; full standalone protocol and SAP attachment are not in stored registry snapshot. Do not interpret one positive trial as proof all program trials succeeded.

findings: FORWARD-4 used sequential parallel-comparison design, randomization, double blinding and placebo control at 54 sites; adjunctive buprenorphine/samidorphan plus continuing antidepressant therapy.
Primary MADRS-10 change at Week 5 did not meet significance: least-squares mean difference -1.8, 95% CI -4.1 to 0.4, P=0.109.
Later exploratory or post-hoc significant EOT measures must not be substituted for the original primary comparison.
records.limitations: Peer-reviewed paper is not a complete original protocol or full SAP attachment; other outcomes should be examined for multiplicity and selection effects.

findings: FORWARD-3 used a double-blind placebo run-in and then six-week randomized adjunctive BUP/SAM 2 mg/2 mg versus placebo for nonresponders at 58 study sites (49 in US, nine in Bulgaria).
Original MADRS-10 primary analysis showed mean change -4.8 vs -4.6 (difference -0.3, P=0.782), not meeting its primary objective.
At least one treatment-emergent adverse event: 42.9% of treated versus 34.5% placebo participants in the stated efficacy-treatment period.
records.limitations: Different placebo run-in from FORWARD-4/5 SPCD. Publication and registry are not evidence of a downloaded complete protocol or SAP.
